quote: Yet often the mountain gives itself most completely when I have no destination, when I reach nowhere in particular, but have gone out merely to be with the mountain as one visits a friend with no intention but to be with him.
source: Nan Shepherd, The Living Mountain, chapter 2, The Recesses (Canongate, 2011), p. 15; first published 1977

evidence.where: I fetched the page-by-page reader of the Canongate 2011 paperback at readingandwalking.ca, which prints the sentence verbatim with its leading Yet, places it in chapter 2, The Recesses, and cites it as page 15. A web search returned the same wording across independent quotation pages. The printed page itself is not openable: both archive.org copies are lending-restricted.
evidence.edition: The Living Mountain: A Celebration of the Cairngorm Mountains of Scotland (Canongate, 2011); first published Aberdeen University Press, 1977
evidence.locator: Chapter 2, The Recesses, p. 15 of the Canongate 2011 text
